subject: What's on in E2 · 15–21 October: a free Sebright bill and Somali Week
preheader: A free three-band bill at the Sebright, comedy and Lynch videos, a sauna rave and the first Halloween dates.

items.blurb: Three bands of dream punk, post punk and grunge in the Sebright's basement gig room, and it costs nothing to get in. An easy yes for a Thursday.

sections.heading: Nights worth crossing the road for
sections.lede: Two Saturdays and a Friday, none of them far from the tube.

items.headline: Margo Marshall at the Working Men's Club
items.blurb: A late club night at the Working Men's Club with Margo Marshall in the line-up. Advance tickets start at £8, and it runs until 2am.

items.headline: Psychedelic shamanic funk at Rich Mix
items.blurb: Part of a K-Music Festival, with the genre listed as psychedelic shamanic funk. One for the curious, in a charity-run arts centre rather than a pub back room.

items.headline: A Friday party at The George Tavern
items.blurb: A Friday DJ night at The George Tavern with Cape Orange, Lifeloose and Jøseph on the bill. Tickets start at £7.50, which is fair for a night out.
A weekly stand-up night at the purpose-built comedy club on Cambridge Heath Road. Tickets from £8.25 make it a cheap way to get a laugh midweek.
The first day of a ten-day Somali arts and culture festival at Oxford House. It is listed as free, but the festival page says to check each event for its own price.
A Tuesday evening of David Lynch music videos at the Working Men's Club. One for film fans, and for Lynch fans in particular.
Free downtempo DJ sessions on Thursdays at 26 Curtain Road, outside our patch but a pleasant way to end a week of work.

notes_for_fred: Pick is the free Sebright bill on Thursday 15 Oct, the day the email goes out, so some readers will see it late. Alternative: BRAT 2 SCHOOL at the Working Men's Club on Saturday.
Many events have no price listed (sauna rave, history workshop, Lynch videos); blurbs say nothing about cost for those.
Somali Week is listed as free, but the festival page says to check each event for its price; the blurb says so.
Strictly Vinyl is outer zone and the only worth-the-trip item; it is also on Thursday, the issue day.
Gallery runs left out under the run rule; all have unlisted prices. SEND Play at Young V&A is the first Saturday of the month, so not this week.
19 events in 8 sections. Community has no section of its own: the free Somali craft workshop sits in Free and under a tenner, and the history workshop (Seeking Liberation, Sat) was left out.
